the Lax equation associated to a (1, 1) tensor on a supermanifolds is a necessary and sufficient condition for integrable fermionic Hamiltonian systems.

(a) a fermionic bi-Hamiltonian system is defined on a supermanifolds and (b) if the Nijenhuis torsion vanishes, all conserved quantities of the system are in involution, which is a sufficient criterion for the system to be integrable.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the bi‐Hamiltonian approach to fermionic integrable models is a very natural extension of the well‐known bi‐Hamiltonian formulation in the bosonic case.

the fermionic Hamiltonian systems with a bi‐linear Poisson bracket can be naturally formulated on a super‐manifold and the corresponding Nijehuis tensor is the obstruction to integrability of such systems.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the Lax equation associated to the fermionic Hamiltonian systems is defined in terms of the supermanifold structure of the system and not in terms of the usual Lax matrix.
